Sasha: Heads-up — saw a regression on FlashX paged-attn for long context (seq=8192). Throughput down ~18% on main after the tiler rework (commit abc123). Memory bandwidth looks very high (near peak). Anyone seen this pattern?

Liam: Which benchmark/runner? canary or full perf harness?

Sasha: Repro locally with `scripts/bench/flashx_paged.sh --seq 8192 --bs 1 --model llama-7b`
Output snippet:
```
throughput: 120 tok/s
bandwidth: 930 GB/s
smem per block: 96KB
```

Maria: Huh. 930 GB/s is suspicious. Could be shared-mem spilling or poor tiling increasing global traffic. Can you paste `nvprof --metrics gld_throughput,gst_throughput,sm_efficiency`?

Sasha: Ran nvprof quick: `gld_throughput=220GB/s, gst_throughput=700GB/s, sm_efficiency=0.60`

Carlos: GST >> GLD implies we're write dominated — maybe KV paging is thrashing or extra writes from pipeline bookkeeping. Is KV hitrate low?

Sasha: KV hit rate is 98% but eviction spikes align with the rollouts. The new tiler increases SM usage per CTA so fewer CTAs fit and we lose locality for KV buffers.

Liam: Try reducing tile_k (tile size in K dim) to 64 and drop pipeline stages 3->2. That bumped occupancy for me last week: 38% -> 62%.

Sasha: Quick experiment with `tile_k=64` and `stages=2`: throughput -> 145 tok/s, bandwidth -> 720 GB/s. Looks promising.

Maria: Good. Also try routing to the fused-attn fallback `runtime --kernel=fused_fast` — it uses less SM and sometimes avoids the high GST path.

Sasha: Fallback fused gives 152 tok/s. Latency tail gets worse under bursty traffic though, maybe due to kernel switching causing KV reinit.

Carlos: That's the danger — kernel oscillation can force KV cache reallocation. We should add hysteresis to routing: only switch kernels if improvement >=10% sustained over 5s (or N requests).

Maria: +1. And add a microbenchmark to the perf infra that simulates realistic skew (e.g., 90% seq=512, 10% seq=8192) so we don't regress on mixed workloads.

Sasha: Plan: open PR to (1) change paged-flashx defaults on A100+ to `tile_k=64, stages=2` and (2) add routing hysteresis at runtime. Will include reproduction script and nvprof output. Assigning to myself, will request review from @Liam and @Maria.

Liam: Ping @eng-runtime for visibility and tag the perf job.

perf-bot: Scheduled job `perf/regress/1919012345-run` queued. ETA ~45m :gear:

Maria: Nice. Also add a note in CHANGELOG about temporary knob so infra teams know why defaults changed.

Sasha: Will do. Thanks all :pray:
